title: Choose your next small step
description: Use the learning paths and lesson exercises to build practical AI knowledge at your own pace.

sections.title: Start with your immediate goal
sections.body: Choose foundations if the concepts feel unfamiliar, practical skills if you have a task in mind, or career guidance if you are deciding what to learn next. The homepage highlights a short beginner route. These paths are suggestions, not entry requirements or qualifications.
bullets: Read the summary before opening a longer guide.
Skip familiar material and return when you need it.

sections.title: Practice before moving on
sections.body: Each guide includes a worked example and a small exercise. Use public or invented information and check the result yourself. If an exercise feels difficult, return to the relevant section or try a simpler example. Understanding one task well is more useful than rushing through several pages.
bullets: Write down one thing you learned.
Keep a note of a question that still needs an answer.

sections.title: Check understanding and revisit gaps
sections.body: Quizzes provide feedback on selected concepts. They are learning tools, not certifications or employment assessments. Review the explanations, return to the linked lessons, and try a new example. Your browser bookmarks can help you keep track of pages you want to revisit.
bullets: Retake a quiz after reviewing its explanations.
Use real-world practice to complement quiz results.

example.title: A practical route
example.text: For a workplace goal, read the privacy guide, learn the prompt structure, and choose a task-specific guide. Complete its exercise before exploring automation.

exercise: Pick one learning outcome for this week and bookmark two relevant lessons.

faq.question: Is there a required order?
faq.answer: No. The beginner route is a suggestion. You can choose lessons based on your interests and current knowledge.

faq.question: Will completing a path give me a certificate?
faq.answer: This learning center does not issue a certificate. It provides free lessons, exercises, and knowledge checks.
